question: Should OpenClaw adopt an opt-in shared durable recovery layer in core, including the `durable.mode` startup and session-handoff contract, before merging this cumulative recovery implementation?
rationale: The patch is not a bounded repair of an established behavior: it introduces a new persistent recovery authority, configuration surface, and fail-closed startup behavior whose long-term ownership and supported upgrade contract require maintainer intent.

options.title: Sponsor the owner-first core boundary
options.body: Accept the narrow durable authority direction and ask for the stack to be rebased and reviewed as ordered current-main slices with upgrade proof.

options.title: Keep recovery owner-specific
options.body: Reject the shared durable layer and request narrowly scoped improvements in the existing task, subagent, flow, and session owners.

options.title: Narrow the proposal first
options.body: Require a smaller accepted RFC scope before deciding whether any shared storage or authority belongs in core.

recommendation.title: Sponsor the owner-first core boundary
recommendation.body: Accept the narrow durable authority direction and ask for the stack to be rebased and reviewed as ordered current-main slices with upgrade proof.

likelyOwner.reason: The supplied history identifies this person as the durable-series author and the best available routing contact; upstream product sponsorship still requires a repository maintainer.
